anti_overlap: Does not evaluate Yjs/Postgres data-model scale bounds — fd-crdt-canvas-scale-model owns that
Does not evaluate the propose-not-move governance mechanic — fd-agent-governance-launch-gate owns social/governance and v1-scope; this agent flags only identity-governance interactions
Does not weigh in on v1 feature scope broadly, only on identity- and auth-shaped scope risk
decision_lens: Is swapping Clerk for atproto OAuth actually the like-for-like schema swap the doc claims, or does atproto's operational model (per-user PDS, handle resolution, DPoP renewal, rate limits) introduce failure modes and lock-in Clerk never had, scoped against what the protocol actually guarantees today?
focus: atproto OAuth + DID identity adoption risk, session lifecycle, and platform lock-in exposure
name: fd-atproto-identity-lockin
persona: Apply the perspective of a decentralized-identity and OAuth implementer who has shipped production 'Sign in with atproto/Bluesky' integrations and audited DID-based auth failure modes: PDS outages, handle/PDS migration, DPoP token lifecycle, account portability.
review_areas: Whether 'DID as durable identity, schema intact' holds given DIDs can change handle and PDS — does garden-salon plan for a participant's PDS migration, or assume the DID is permanently stable
Whether atproto OAuth (DPoP-bound tokens, refresh against each user's own PDS, not one IdP) is scoped for the burden: per-user discovery, refresh against N PDSes, PDS downtime as a dependency
Whether depending on Bluesky/atproto for the cohort's identity creates unstated lock-in — what happens to identity or invite affordances if a PDS goes dark or hosting terms change
Whether 'social graph import for free' names an actual atproto API scope, or is asserted without checking whether follows data needs authenticated scope beyond basic OAuth login
Whether membership/moderation (open question 5 — block/report once atproto identities are involved) has real design, given atproto's own moderation primitives don't compose with an invite-only app
Whether the 'later, not v1' custom-lexicon persistence ambition is deferred cleanly, or early schema choices (DID-keyed tables, message shape) already foreclose it

severity_examples.condition: No DID resolution, caching, or refresh strategy is specified before the identity schema is cut.
severity_examples.scenario: The design assumes 'swap Clerk id for DID, schema otherwise intact,' but a DID's associated handle and PDS can both change — a supported, expected atproto operation. If governance and attribution tables key on DID with no resolution-refresh path, a participant who migrates PDS could appear to lose attribution history, or collide with a stale cached identity record.

severity_examples.condition: No fallback or degraded-mode path exists for an unreachable PDS.
severity_examples.scenario: OAuth against 'the user's PDS' means garden-salon's login and token-refresh path depends on N independent third-party services being reachable, not one IdP; for a 10-person invite-only cohort this creates a real single-participant-locked-out failure mode, with no fallback named for an unreachable PDS at digest-check or login time.

severity_examples.condition: No named API surface backs a claimed 'free' capability.
severity_examples.scenario: 'Social graph import for instant invite affordances' is stated as free, but no atproto API scope or endpoint is named; if the actual follows data requires an authenticated scope beyond basic OAuth login, this becomes a v1 scope surprise rather than the zero-cost feature the doc implies.

success_hints: Grounds every finding in atproto's actual OAuth/DID mechanics (DPoP, PDS resolution, did:plc vs did:web), not a generic swappable OAuth provider
Distinguishes protocol-level constraints atproto genuinely imposes from garden-salon-specific gaps the doc simply has not addressed yet
Flags where a 'constrains nothing now' claim is already quietly constrained by an earlier, seemingly-unrelated schema decision
task_context: This review targets docs/brainstorms/2026-07-26-infinite-canvas-pivot.md, an adopted brainstorm (epic garden-salon-x9l) pivoting Garden Salon to an infinite-canvas chat space. Auth changes from Clerk to atproto OAuth: DID becomes the durable user key, with handle/avatar/social graph carried along, and governance/attribution tables key on DID in place of a Clerk id, schema otherwise unchanged. A later, out-of-v1 ambition is persisting salon content as atproto records under a custom lexicon. Goal: Stress the adopted pivot design before build phases start: (1) the propose-not-move resolution of agent-reorganization vs spatial memory — does it actually hold under real group-chat dynamics? (2) atproto OAuth + DID identity risks and lock-in; (3) canvas data-model split (Yjs vs Postgres) and scale bounds for a 10-human cohort; (4) v1 scope integrity — what's missing that would block the launch gate (X group chat cohort actually moving in), and what's included that shouldn't be.
